Server-only flow step: `- run: delete_upload` with `with: { path: '${{ steps.lookup.outputs.file_url }}' }` (a whole flow: deletion_example). The path is interpolated, must be a reference produced by this app's selected storage backend, and backend failures stop the flow. This key covers private files; a public file is deleted only with `record:` (public_deletion).

Authorize first: use `auth: required` and select the stored reference through an ownership/tenant-scoped SQL step. Never pass a request parameter directly to delete_upload; path confinement proves storage scope, not row ownership. Name the owning row with `record: { table, id }` (read before the row is deleted) and the step also applies the uploader rule (private_ownership); without `with.record` the rule is advisory (logged).

Only canonical `uploads/private/...` refs (optional leading slash), this instance's exact managed-CDN private URL (a dev instance's is under `<sub>-dev`; see dev_instance_prefix), or this app's exact configured-S3 private URL are accepted. Foreign-app, query/fragment, traversal, encoded, and unknown-host references fail before I/O (a public reference follows public_deletion), and so does any other spelling of a stored URL (a doubled slash such as `/private/<app>//uploads/private/x`, or an uppercase scheme), and on local disk any spelling other than the one the file is stored under (file_identity). Missing objects succeed for safe retries.

In `transaction: true`, place delete_upload before the metadata DELETE so a storage failure prevents that SQL commit. SQLite rolls back when deletion fails and skips later steps, but object deletion is external and cannot be restored if later SQL/commit fails; keep retries idempotent and never claim DB+object atomicity.

Deleting the object also ends every signed link already handed out for it, at once: the link answers 403 on the media CDN (404 on local storage) from then on, whatever lifetime it was signed for. That is the only way to end a signed link before its expiry (api({at:'signed-urls'}) → revocation).
